doors.label: The parlour
doors.lockedLine: Sealed by the Sergeant: tell him what the hall told you first, and the parlour opens.

doors.label: Kitchen passage
doors.lockedLine: The kitchen passage is dark, and the Sergeant has it taped until the parlour's account closes.

doors.label: The stairs
doors.lockedLine: The stairs go up into a taped-off dark. Close the parlour's account first.

hints.tier1: Something in this hall keeps time. What stopped when the storm struck, and what does the open book by the door have to say about visitors?
hints.tier2: The grandfather clock died at 10:47 when the power failed. Set that against the ledger: one visitor, gone by a quarter past ten. Then check the umbrella he left behind -- dry, in the stand.
hints.tier3: The hall says: only Julian used the front door, and he left at a quarter past ten. The clock fixes the blackout at 10:47. The mat and the dry umbrella agree. Say it to the parlour door.

hints.tier1: He was reading when it took him. What was he reading, what is missing from it -- and what does a dull film inside a glass mean?
hints.tier2: Take the magnifier to the glass, the decanter and the ember's edge. Read the garden door's bolt. Mind the rug by the fender: rain-damp feet, and nobody in the house wears treads like those.
hints.tier3: Foxglove in the decanter -- not his glass. Burned stems in the hearth, two petals missed. A diamond-tread print, size seven to eight, by the fender. The garden door stood off its bolt all through the dark. Say it to the hall.

doors.label: Down the cellar stair
doors.lockedLine: The cellar stair is dark, and the Sergeant has it taped until the study's papers have told their truth.

hints.tier1: The kitchen bakes its own alibi: the loaf, the wireless, the lantern -- and the flags by the garden door remember feet.
hints.tier2: A loaf burnt -- not raw -- says the oven came back without her. The wireless sang to an empty room when the power returned. The lantern's oil measures her dark half hour. Take the magnifier to the stone flags by the garden door, and open the second book on the dresser.
hints.tier3: The dark ran 10:47 to 11:21: bread in at 10:35, lantern lit, wireless dead mid-song -- then singing again at 11:21 to nobody. Diamond-tread prints, rain-wet, cross the flags from the garden door toward the hall. Her rounds book has the door off its bolt at half eleven. The kitchen clears Colette -- and dates the visitor.

hints.tier1: The study kept the argument, the plea, and the safe. The desk, the basket and the wall behind the fox know all three.
hints.tier2: The blotter wants the torch: pencil pressure reads where ink never reached. The waste basket keeps what paper people crumple. Behind the fox engraving there is a door of another kind -- and a journal upstairs names its key.
hints.tier3: Julian begged in pencil at ten past ten and cabbed away at 10:19. The safe keeps carbons of pages 40 to 43 -- the confession survives. And on the work shelf, an apprentice's tin answers for a button.

doors.label: Peggy's room
doors.lockedLine: Peggy's door is shut. It opens when the dark half hour has its arithmetic.

doors.label: Edmund's room
doors.lockedLine: His room keeps his past folded away -- it opens when the dark half hour has its arithmetic.

doors.label: The bathroom
doors.lockedLine: The medicine shelves wait behind a door the Sergeant still tapes.

doors.label: Up to the attic
doors.lockedLine: The attic stair is taped and dark. The papers must be read before anyone climbs.

hints.tier1: The landing hears everything and says little -- but the carpet lanes and a sill of washed glass keep habits.
hints.tier2: The stair runner wears lanes worn by years of the same feet, and fresh candle wax on the twelfth step. Outside Peggy's door: her tonic bottle and a rinsed glass, drying unhurried.
hints.tier3: The runner's lanes are habit's map -- Edmund's stick, Colette's trays, and Tobias's midnight candle carried down. The rinsed tonic glass says Peggy settled for the night. Nobody's story here is a stranger's story -- the stranger never used the stairs.

hints.tier1: A novel, a candle, and a burn that stops at eleven.
hints.tier2: Take the magnifier to the candle's wax ridge and read where the flame died. The writing case on the table keeps the day's post -- and its red stamp.
hints.tier3: Her candle burned exactly to the eleven-o'clock mark: asleep long before any clock could have wound. The final notice is hers alone, and Tuesday's letter frightens a debtor, not a murderer.

hints.tier1: He kept the past in this room, folded.
hints.tier2: The journal on the nightstand names the past: a first name, a surname, and where its pages sleep. Mind the ribbon.
hints.tier3: Ruth Marsh drew the fox first. The journal names the safe, and the little key hangs on the ribbon -- the study wall keeps what the fire never saw.

hints.tier2: Open the cabinet: three shelves, one hand. Read the labels, then the receipt book on the washstand.
hints.tier3: The doctor restocks this cabinet monthly -- iron and quinine, aspirin, and Edmund's digitalis, nearly full. Everything here is ordinary: the drops were not the vehicle.

hints.tier1: Two people worked in this room, years apart. One of them is not who the books say.
hints.tier2: Ruth's shelf keeps her sketchbooks -- the dates will do, and the last page needs no glass. The key board by the stair has an empty hook. On Tobias's desk a line stops mid-stroke, and his portfolio keeps what the published pages cover.
hints.tier3: The sketchbooks are dated years before Whistler, and the last page reads 'H. carried the light away -- R.' The key is gone from its hook: he carried it down to the parlour that night. The candle stub sat wedged in the door frame since 1949, the stair door was bolted from the landing side, and the ghost drafts and tea-aged copies say the apprentice's line was the published line.

doors.label: Up the stair to the kitchen

hints.tier1: The cellar answers one question only: how many ways in?
hints.tier2: The coal hatch is the house's other door. Take the magnifier to its mouth and read the dust.
hints.tier3: The dust in the chute mouth lies whole and unbroken: nobody came or went by the coal hatch, carrying anything. The garden door was the visitor's only road.

hints.tier1: Where the washing lives, the household's secrets dry flat.
hints.tier2: The shelf above the copper keeps a biscuit tin that has not held biscuits for months. Tobias sleeps at the end of the room -- his candle tin banks the wick he carries up and down the stairs.
hints.tier3: In the tin: the housekeeping money, short for months, and the page she tore out of the account book. Colette skimmed the tin for her sister's debts and hid the shame with it. It was never the door she lied about -- she has bolted that door for thirty-one years.
